newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour sees support slip in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour sees support slip in latest poll.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party is 18 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives but its lead has fallen by six points over the past month, according to the latest Gallup poll.
A survey for Friday's Daily Telegraph newspaper puts Labour on 50.5 percent with the Conservatives on 32.5 percent, while the minority Liberal Democrats are trailing at 10.5 percent.
Prime Minister John Major must call an election by May.

But month-on-month comparisons are affected by the fact that Gallup has changed its method of testing opinion since its last poll for the Telegraph. It has moved to random telephone sampling after having used face-to-face interviews for years.
The Daily Telegraph said the old method of street interviews tended to exaggerate Labour support at the expense of the Conservatives because it reached too many working class voters.
Gallup estimates that Labour's lead has shrunk by six points over the past month with the Conservatives up four points from 28.5 percent and Labour down two points from 52.5 percent.
Support for the Liberal Democrats has fallen by one point over the past month.
Labour spokesman Brian Wilson said comparison with the December figures could not be treated as valid.

"Effectively, this is a new poll conducted using relatively untried methodology. It should therefore be compared not with the December Gallup poll, but the polls carried out over the last month by other polling organisations in other newspapers."
Labour needs a 4.3 percent swing from the Conservatives at the election to obtain an overall majority. The swing at present, according to Friday's poll, is 12.8 percent to Labour.
